page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network interfaces with a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression. However, the 64-vCPU allocation delivers average multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable strength, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET performance, consistently register in the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.16xlarge offers a high density of dedicated compute resources without the added expense of bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. This makes it a balanced choice for parallelizable workloads that can leverage its 64 vCPUs. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded data decompression, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks that do not require GPU acceleration.
